name: Toronto
tagline: Canada's largest and most multicultural city, a genuine United Nations of neighbourhoods anchored by a tower that dominated the world's skylines for over three decades.
highlight: Standing on the CN Tower's glass floor, 342 metres of open air the only thing between your feet and the street below.
shortDescription: Canada's largest and most multicultural city, home to the CN Tower, the Distillery District's Victorian warehouses and neighbourhoods representing the world.
metaDescription: A Toronto travel guide: the CN Tower, the Distillery District, Kensington Market, Casa Loma, food and how to plan a visit to Canada's biggest city.
knownFor: The CN Tower, Kensington Market, the Distillery District

intro: Toronto is genuinely Canada's largest city and its most multicultural, with over half its population born outside Canada and neighbourhoods representing nearly every corner of the world.
Its skyline is genuinely still defined by the CN Tower, which held the record for the world's tallest freestanding structure for more than three decades.
The real draw, though, is genuinely street level — Kensington Market's eclectic shops, the Distillery District's Victorian warehouses, and a food scene that reflects the city's remarkable diversity.

whyVisit.intro: Toronto's case rests genuinely on being one of the world's most diverse cities, with the food and neighbourhood culture to prove it.

points.title: It's genuinely one of the most multicultural cities on Earth
points.text: Neighbourhoods representing dozens of cultures, each with its own genuine character.

points.title: The CN Tower is genuinely still an icon
points.text: A defining symbol of the skyline, with a glass floor and revolving restaurant.

points.title: The food scene is genuinely exceptional
points.text: A direct reflection of the city's diversity, from dim sum to Jamaican patties to fine dining.

points.title: It's genuinely a real, walkable big city
points.text: Distinct neighbourhoods connect easily by transit or on foot.

points.title: It works genuinely well as an Eastern Canada base
points.text: An easy pairing with Niagara Falls, Montreal and Quebec City.

attractionsIntro: Toronto's essential sights are genuinely spread across its downtown core and a handful of distinct historic neighbourhoods.

attractions.name: The CN Tower

image.file: File:CN Tower, Toronto, Canada (Unsplash DJ kOgH5u0o).jpg

attractions.text: Genuinely the city's defining landmark, held the record for the world's tallest freestanding structure from 1975 to 2007.
attractions.tip: Genuinely book a sunset time slot for the best light over Lake Ontario.

attractions.name: The Distillery District
attractions.text: Genuinely a car-free enclave of Victorian industrial architecture, once the largest whisky distillery in the British Empire.
attractions.tip: Genuinely a lovely spot for a slow wander among galleries, boutiques and cafés.

attractions.name: Casa Loma

image.alt: Casa Loma, a castle in Toronto

attractions.text: Genuinely a full-scale early 20th-century castle, complete with secret passages and manicured gardens.
attractions.tip: Genuinely allow a couple of hours to properly explore both the interior and the grounds.

attractions.name: St Lawrence Market

image.file: File:St Lawrence Market, Toronto, West partial view 20170417 1.jpg

attractions.text: Genuinely a working market with real history, once named the world's best food market by National Geographic.
attractions.tip: Genuinely visit on a Saturday for the additional farmers' market in the north building.

attractions.name: Kensington Market
attractions.text: Genuinely one of the city's most eclectic neighbourhoods, vintage shops and global food stalls packed into a few colourful blocks.
attractions.tip: Genuinely visit on a car-free Pedestrian Sunday if your dates align, held on the last Sunday of warmer months.

attractions.name: The Toronto Islands

image.file: File:View of Toronto Skyline from Centre Island.jpg
image.alt: Toronto's skyline seen from the Toronto Islands

attractions.text: Genuinely a car-free escape a short ferry ride from downtown, with beaches, parkland and the city's best skyline view.
attractions.tip: Genuinely rent a bike on the islands to cover more ground than walking alone.

attractions.name: The Royal Ontario Museum's Crystal

image.alt: The Michael Lee-Chin Crystal at the Royal Ontario Museum

attractions.text: Genuinely a striking architectural statement, a jagged crystalline extension bursting from the museum's original heritage building.
attractions.tip: Genuinely allow a full afternoon — the collection inside is genuinely extensive.

thingsToDoIntro: Toronto genuinely rewards exploring by neighbourhood, each with its own distinct food and character.

thingsToDo.title: Go up the CN Tower

image.file: File:Toronto - ON - CN Tower bei Nacht2.jpg

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely essential Toronto experience, taking in the view from the observation deck or glass floor.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely consider the EdgeWalk if you want a real adrenaline rush — a hands-free walk around the tower's outer rim.

thingsToDo.title: Wander the Distillery District's cobblestones

image.alt: Cobblestone streets in the Distillery District

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely relaxed way to spend an afternoon, browsing boutiques and galleries in converted Victorian warehouses.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely check the events calendar — the district regularly hosts markets and festivals.

thingsToDo.title: Tour Casa Loma's castle rooms
thingsToDo.text: A genuinely fun, slightly surreal visit, wandering a full-scale castle's period rooms and secret tunnel.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely check for seasonal light shows and special events held on the grounds.

thingsToDo.title: Browse St Lawrence Market's food stalls

image.alt: Food stalls at St Lawrence Market

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely essential food stop, sampling everything from peameal bacon sandwiches to international specialties.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely go hungry and share several stalls' offerings rather than filling up at just one.

thingsToDo.title: Explore Kensington Market's eclectic shops
thingsToDo.text: A genuinely colourful way to spend a few hours, vintage stores and global street food packed into a compact area.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely pair with neighbouring Chinatown, just a short walk away.

thingsToDo.title: Take the ferry to the Toronto Islands

image.file: File:Toronto Islands Yacht Club and Skyline.jpg
image.alt: The ferry to the Toronto Islands

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely easy, scenic escape, swapping downtown streets for beaches and the city's best skyline photo.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely book ferry tickets online ahead on busy summer weekends.

foodIntro: Toronto's food genuinely reflects its remarkable diversity, a real strength of the city's dining scene.

foods.name: Peameal bacon sandwich

image.alt: A peameal bacon sandwich, a Toronto specialty

foods.text: Genuinely a true Toronto original, cornmeal-crusted back bacon piled onto a soft bun.
foods.whereToTry: St Lawrence Market's Carousel Bakery, the dish's most famous source.

foods.name: Jamaican beef patty
foods.text: Genuinely a beloved staple reflecting Toronto's large Caribbean community.
foods.whereToTry: Bakeries and shops throughout the city, especially in Caribbean neighbourhoods.

foods.name: Butter tarts

image.file: File:Butter tarts it's a Canadian thing. (47104703864).jpg
image.alt: Butter tarts, a classic Canadian pastry

foods.text: Genuinely a beloved Ontario classic, found at bakeries throughout the city.

foods.name: Poutine

image.alt: Poutine, Canada's fries, cheese curds and gravy dish

foods.text: Genuinely widely available, though this is Quebec's dish rather than a local specialty.
foods.whereToTry: Restaurants and food trucks throughout the city.

foods.name: Dim sum

image.file: File:Three dim sum in steamer basket.jpg

foods.text: Genuinely excellent here too, a reflection of Toronto's own large Chinese community.

foods.name: Ontario craft beer and wine
foods.text: Genuinely worth exploring, with a thriving local brewery scene and Niagara wine country nearby.
foods.whereToTry: Bars and restaurants throughout the city.

accommodation.intro: Toronto genuinely offers accommodation for every budget, with downtown commanding the highest prices.

areas.name: Downtown or the Entertainment District
areas.bestFor: Being genuinely within walking distance of the CN Tower and waterfront
areas.text: The most convenient, though also the priciest, part of the city to stay.

areas.name: Queen West or Kensington
areas.bestFor: A genuinely more character-filled, slightly better value stay
areas.text: Close to Kensington Market and Chinatown, with easy transit downtown.

gettingThere.intro: Toronto is genuinely one of North America's best-connected cities by air, with a large international airport.

options.text: Genuinely available from across the world.
options.detail: The UP Express train connects Pearson Airport to downtown Union Station in about 25 minutes.
Via Rail's corridor service connects all three cities well.

options.mode: Bus or drive from Niagara Falls
options.detail: About 1.5 hours by road or a direct GO Transit train.

gettingAround.intro: Toronto's genuinely extensive transit network covers the city well, with downtown itself easily walkable.

options.text: Genuinely reliable and easy to use across the city.
options.detail: The TTC's subway lines and streetcar network cover most major sights.

options.text: Genuinely the best way to explore individual downtown neighbourhoods.
options.detail: Kensington Market, the Distillery District and the waterfront are all walkable once you're there.

options.text: Genuinely the only way to reach the islands.
options.detail: Frequent departures from the downtown ferry terminal.

bestTime.headline: May to September for warm weather and outdoor events
bestTime.summary: Toronto is genuinely a year-round city, with summer bringing the most festivals and outdoor activity.

seasons.text: Genuinely mild, comfortable weather before summer's full heat and humidity arrive.
Genuinely warm and humid, with the city's festival calendar in full swing.
Genuinely comfortable temperatures with excellent fall colour in the city's parks.
Genuinely cold, with the city's extensive PATH underground walkway system a real asset.

bestTime.avoid: Genuinely nothing strongly — Toronto genuinely works as a year-round city break.

days.evening: Dinner and drinks in the Distillery District.

days.title: Neighbourhoods and Casa Loma
days.summary: A day of distinct city character.
days.afternoon: Tour Casa Loma's castle rooms and gardens.
days.evening: Dinner reflecting the city's global food scene.

days.title: The Toronto Islands
days.summary: A relaxed day on the water.
days.afternoon: Cycle or walk the islands, with the skyline view.

tipsIntro: Practical notes that make a Toronto visit noticeably smoother.
tips: Book genuinely CN Tower tickets online ahead, especially for sunset time slots.
Use genuinely the PATH underground walkway system in winter to avoid the cold.
Explore genuinely by neighbourhood — Toronto's real character lives outside downtown's tower district.
Book genuinely Toronto Islands ferry tickets ahead on busy summer weekends.
Try genuinely food from multiple different neighbourhoods rather than sticking to downtown alone.
Use genuinely Toronto as a base for day trips to Niagara Falls.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Toronto?
faq.a: Three days genuinely covers the city's main sights and a couple of its distinct neighbourhoods comfortably.
Genuinely comparable to other major North American cities, with food covering a wide range of budgets.
Yes, genuinely — downtown and its surrounding neighbourhoods are compact and well served by transit.

faq.q: Is the CN Tower worth visiting?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely — it remains an iconic experience, and the glass floor is genuinely a memorable thrill.

faq.q: Can you day-trip to Niagara Falls from Toronto?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely easily — it's about 1.5 hours by road or a direct train.
Yes, genuinely exceptional — its multicultural population makes it one of North America's best cities for diverse, authentic cuisine.
